key_insight: Gas-phase anion exchange enables continuous, reversible tuning of visible BIC resonances by more than 40 nm in halide-perovskite metasurfaces.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables post-fabrication control of compact lasers and adaptive meta-optics, rather than demonstrating AI or solar-cell performance.
method: Fabricate MAPbBr₃ metasurfaces using nanoimprint lithography.
Expose them to HCl vapor to replace some bromide with chloride, lowering refractive index and blueshifting resonances.
Apply HBr vapor to reverse the exchange and restore the initial resonance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports greater-than-40-nm BIC resonance tuning, minute-timescale material changes, and continuous reversible tuning of BIC-mediated lasing from the same metasurface.
watch_item: Long-term cycling stability and practical handling of corrosive HCl/HBr vapors remain implementation concerns not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Gas-induced reversible spectral tuning of bound states in the continuum in perovskite metasurfaces
